initial_test_run:
First run: the plain-text fixture failed (its header line has no label column, so naive cell positions misaligned); plain-text cells now keep character offsets and headers align by overlap. Five lifecycle tests then failed because the frozen Cache does not create its root; the probe now creates attempts//source first. 'Three and Six Months Ended' parsed as six months; a shared-duration rule fixed it. A review before freezing then made these changes, each covered by a new or updated test (written with the change, not run against the earlier code): the attempt check moved under the study lock, a projection interrupted before it was written is completed on resume, --reanalyze accepts only a complete attempt of the frozen definition, an equal value is dropped as a different period only on a contradicting end date or duration (otherwise period_unverified), a bare year-to-date header takes the 10-Q's year-to-date length, plain-text headers skip section labels, table context is limited to text since the previous table, and a stacked mid-table period header starts a new header block. The frozen-identity test failed until freeze.json existed; then all 31 passed. Before that freeze was published, the Codex review of the previous push raised nine findings, addressed with new tests and a re-freeze: an unsigned amount under a 'net loss' or 'cash used' label is negative (one new assertion first failed because an unsigned amount was accepted with either sign; the rule now makes it negative only) and 'Net (loss) income' labels match; narrative amounts pair with the label and period of their own clause, and a clause naming an excluded measure does not count; rowspan is expanded; the spot-check membership rule is declared; a header missing identity fields is identity_unverified (lower bound only) rather than identity_failed; ambiguous releases and currency_mismatch no longer count in the upper bound by themselves. The header-identity test failed once as expected when a missing acceptance moved from issues to missing; then all 35 passed. Second review round (on the published freeze 67529c4c), nine findings, each covered by a new or updated test and followed by a re-freeze: possibly stated outcomes (an unreadable or image-only candidate) now outrank label_only when documents are matched jointly; a statement image counts even after a label appears elsewhere, with stricter statement names; release identification reads text in source order; evidence carries each exhibit's SHA256; summary.json reports per-component shares and Wilson intervals; prose amounts accept USD before or after and a leading minus; several distinct years in one clause with several amounts are period_unverified; footnote text is dropped; and other Python processes running anything under .qualification refuse the start (listed with ps or PowerShell Get-CimInstance; the Windows path is exercised only with a mocked listing here). The new tests passed on their first run; then all 41 passed. Third review round (on 11e4ca33), seven findings, each covered by a new test and followed by a re-freeze: prose in non-data table cells is read as narrative; currency codes in their own cells (before or after the value) and column headers naming another currency give currency_mismatch; image context is the text just before the image in source order, in or out of tables; month-year headers read as the month end; table evidence records the row; 'cash flow from operations' matches operating cash flow and continuing/discontinued-operations labels are excluded; a new attempt's folder appears only by renaming a staging folder that already holds attempt.json. One new assertion failed first (a currency code after the value was consumed as a prefix) and was fixed; then all 46 passed. Fourth review round (on 7434c98c), five findings, each covered by a new or updated test written with the change (not run against the earlier code) and followed by a re-freeze: a single full-row spanning cell can be a stacked period header;
,

and

inside a cell separate words; each narrative amount belongs to the nearest label before it, so an adjusted amount in a GAAP clause is not credited; a value equal only at a scale inferred without a unit phrase is scale_unverified (upper bound only); resume and reanalysis require the attempt's recorded code SHA256s to equal the active freeze. All 50 passed on the first run. Fifth review round (on 07c47a95), five findings, each covered by a new test written with the change and followed by a re-freeze: a caption or context unit phrase naming another currency gives currency_mismatch; a clause naming several durations (quarter and six months) is period_unverified, and 'of fiscal year 2025' no longer counts as a twelve-month duration; the any-EX-99 readout also covers release_unidentified events; a saved transport failure without an acknowledged stop halts again on resume; reanalysis rechecks the timing events, calendar and recorded projection SHA256. All 54 passed. Sixth review round (on a12c4da7), seven findings, each covered by a new test written with the change and followed by a re-freeze: another measure (EBITDA, revenue, EPS, adjusted ...) named between a narrative amount and its label stops the amount from counting; caption/context currency is table-wide while a column header's currency applies to its own column; a projection written but not yet recorded is bound on resume and a changed one is refused; numbered footnotes such as '5.2(1)' are ignored; '(5.2 million USD)' is negative; narrative evidence records the owning label and parsed period; attempt.json keeps the original runtime and records each resume's runtime. All 58 passed.
